title: Flag a clip longer than its words
statement: Flag any narration clip longer than its text predicts, and look for added words before blaming slow delivery, since extra length usually means the voice spoke beyond the script.
example: One eight-word clip ran 16.5 seconds because the voice had spoken its whole style prompt inside it.
detail: A reading course's contract check flags any clip held longer than 3.5 seconds plus 0.75 seconds a word, because that usually means the voice spoke extra words. In a build of 101 clips, a cached eight-word sentence came back with the voice's whole style prompt spoken inside it, 16.5 seconds long, and shipped into every place that speaks the sentence; a sync check caught it playing past its last mark, and a transcript showed the prompt. The fix deletes the cached clip, makes it again and confirms about 0.5 seconds a word and a clean transcript.
against: A long clip is not always extra words: colon enumerations "trigger slow deliberate enumeration; one such clip took 10 fresh syntheses to land in-spec" (`grade3-reading/.claude/skills/tts-clips/SKILL.md`, lines 106-107). The bound is one course's setting. The fix relies on a clean transcript, and a model transcription check can miss spoken extras: of four narration takes that all read their style instruction aloud, it flagged only the one where it heard 230 words against a 90-word script (`g9/narration/auditions/2026-10-06-scene1/gemini-3.8-flash-tts-Algenib/vo_intro_01.transcript.json`, lines 5-6) and passed the other three (`g9/narration/auditions/2026-10-06-scene1/DECISION.md`, line 40), while blind audio judges named all four takes as reading the prompt (`g9/narration/auditions/2026-10-06-scene1/judging/judgments.json`, lines 16 and 157).
